name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (C-visa)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires travel medical insurance covering emergency medical assistance, hospitalisation, and repatriation, with minimum coverage of EUR 30,000, valid for the whole Schengen area for the entire stay.
requirements.fix_path: Purchase qualifying travel medical insurance before applying.

evidence_required.document: Passport (valid 3+ months beyond departure, issued within 10 years, 2+ blank pages)
Proof of purpose of travel, accommodation, and return/onward travel

outcome.duration_length: up to 90 days within any 180-day period; visa validity itself can be issued for longer, single- or multiple-entry

sources.title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Croatia (mvep.gov.hr) -- Supporting documents for Schengen visa

notes: NEW COUNTRY, first Croatia route. Croatia has been a full Schengen member (no internal border checks) since January 2023; this route models the standard short-stay (C-visa) issued for the 90/180-day rule, which is EU-wide (Visa Code), not Croatia-specific -- consistent with how other Schengen-member countries in this dataset handle their own schengen_visitor routes. The 90/180-day limit itself is not restated as a separate sourced requirement here since it defines duration_length rather than a qualifying condition. HONEST GAP: the source fetched in this pass does not specify a daily/lump-sum financial-means figure for Croatia specifically (unlike Estonia's confirmed EUR 70/day) -- not invented here; only the confirmed EUR 30,000 insurance minimum is encoded as a hard requirement. Many nationalities do not need a visa at all for short stays; this route applies only to nationals who do.
